newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan August export orders up 0.03 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan August export orders up 0.03 percent yr/yr.

text.p: Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose 0.03 percent in August from August 1995 to US$10.1 billion, the economics mininstry said on Friday.
The following is a table of export data in millions of U.S. dollar.
Orders from the United States fell 0.50 percent to $3.17 billion. The main decrease was due to slowing orders for electronics products.
Orders from Japan were down 4.14 percent to $1.23 billion due to declining orders of animal and plant products, while Hong Kong orders decreased 5.79 percent to $1.84 billion.
European orders grew 8.76 percent to $1.45 billion on rising demand for information and telecommunication products.
Orders in Taiwan's key information and telecommunications sector increased 14.66 percent to $1.50 billion while electronics orders fell 5.16 percent to $1.43 billion.
Textile orders were down 2.05 percent to $1.34 billion and orders for base metal products decreased 5.80 percent to $845 million.
Machinery orders were up 5.29 percent to $657 million, while those for plastics and rubber products were down 0.46 percent to $654 million.
Orders for transportation tools and equipment grew 5.43 percent to $524 million.
